en.headline: Examinations Authority reports data leak of 16900 mainland exam applicants
en.dek: The Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority said a cybersecurity incident on systems for two international exams exposed names, dates of birth and emails of about 16900 mainland residents.
body: The Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority said it had reported a cybersecurity incident involving part of its international examination information systems to the police and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data.

The authority said the incident, discovered on Thursday, mainly affected personal data of about 16,900 mainland residents who had applied for two international examinations. The data included names, dates of birth and email addresses.

It apologised to those affected and said it had set up a hotline at 3628 8787 and an email address for enquiries. It has also notified the relevant examination organisers and is arranging to contact the individuals concerned.

The authority emphasised that the affected systems were used only for certain small-scale international examinations. The Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination and the majority of other international examinations use separate systems, and there is currently no evidence that they were affected. It is conducting a full inspection and investigation of the systems.

zh.headline: 考評局公布國際考試系統資料外洩 涉約1.69萬名內地申請人
zh.dek: 香港考試及評核局表示，周四發現部分國際考試資訊系統發生網絡安全事故，約1.69萬名申請兩項國際考試的內地居住人士姓名、出生日期及電郵地址外洩。
body: 香港考試及評核局表示，已就一宗涉及部分國際考試資訊系統的網絡安全事故報警，並通報個人資料私隱專員公署，將全力配合調查和跟進工作。
考評局指，事件於周四被發現，主要涉及約16,900名申請兩項國際考試的內地居住人士個人資料外洩，相關資料包括姓名、出生日期及電郵地址。
局方就事件向受影響人士致歉，已設立查詢熱線3628 8787及電郵供查詢，並已通報相關考試主辦機構，正跟進通知受影響人士的安排。
考評局強調，涉事系統只應用於個別小規模國際考試，香港中學文憑考試及絕大部分其他國際考試另設獨立系統，目前未有證據顯示受影響。局方已對相關系統進行全面檢查及深入調查。
